review: 1:4 רָחַץ אוֹתָנוּ מֵחֵטְא — Revelation 1:5 (הַמְּרַחֵץ אוֹתָנוּ מֵחֲטָאֵינוּ בְּדָמוֹ); the Arabic غَسَّلَنَا مِنَ الذُّنُوب is that verse, and רָחַץ is the biblical verb for washing away.
2:1 וֵאלֹהִים הִצְדִּיקָנוּ — Romans 8:33 (אֱלֹהִים הוּא הַמַּצְדִּיק); the Arabic وَاللهُ قَدْ بَرَّرَنَا is that verse, and the hiph'il of צדק is the fixed term for justification.
2:4 וּמִי יַשְׁטִין — 'and who will accuse?' (Rom 8:33–34); שָׂטַן as a verb is the biblical 'to accuse' (Ps 38:21), which keeps the courtroom image.
3:1–3:2 בְּאַהֲבַת בְּנוֹ הֶחָבִיב — 'with the love of His beloved Son'; the Arabic مَحَبَّةَ ابْنِهِ الْحَبِيب is a construct, and Hebrew keeps it although the sense is 'as He loves His Son'.
4:2 טוֹב מִשְׁעָן — 'the best of stays', for نِعْمَ السَّنَد; the Arabic nعْمَ construction has no Hebrew equivalent, so the comparative adjective carries the superlative as in hymn 38.
